briefings.title: 10th Anniversary Keynote | Armand Joulin, Google DeepMind
briefings.tldr: Google has successfully merged DeepMind’s research culture with Google’s engineering scale to create a "breakthrough machine" that balances top-tier proprietary models (Gemini) with a rapidly expanding, community-driven open-source ecosystem (Gemma) aimed at global accessibility and specialized industrial use cases.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Google has successfully merged DeepMind’s research culture with Google’s engineering scale to create a "breakthrough machine" that balances top-tier proprietary models (Gemini) with a rapidly expanding, community-driven open-source ecosystem (Gemma) aimed at global accessibility and specialized industrial use cases.

## The Google-DeepMind "Breakthrough Machine"
*   **Mission-Driven AI:** Google’s core objective is to make AI "helpful for everyone," integrating it into existing infrastructure like Maps and Gmail while simultaneously pushing scientific boundaries in chemistry, climate change, and education.
*   **The Merger Advantage:** The merger of Google Brain and DeepMind created a unique organizational engine. 
    *   **Methodological Legacy:** Using the "AlphaGo" blueprint, the organization focuses on end-to-end project design, from specialized infrastructure to high-level research.
    *   **Development Velocity:** Over the last two years, Google has shifted to a high-speed release cycle, deploying models like Veo (video), Imagen (image generation), and Gemini 2.5 (Pro, Flash, and Flash-Lite).
*   **Universal Integration:** AI is no longer a standalone product but the "fuel" for every Google surface, including Search, Gemini Live, and Deep Research.

## Gemma: Google’s Open-Source Philosophy
*   **Ecosystem Scale:** Since its release, Gemma has seen massive adoption, surpassing 300 million downloads as of October 2024, with current estimates reaching 400–500 million.
*   **Global Reach:** While many AI models are US-centric, Gemma is designed for the global market.
    *   **Language Support:** The model supports over 140 languages to accommodate a user base where 80% of individuals reside outside the United States.
*   **Community-Driven Development:** DeepMind actively iterates on Gemma by soliciting feedback from the open-source community to identify performance gaps and required features, such as larger context windows.

## Technical Innovations in Gemma 3
*   **Native Multimodality:** Unlike previous iterations, the latest models are natively multimodal, capable of processing and reasoning across text and images simultaneously.
*   **Audio-First for Mobile:** The smallest Gemma models now include audio capabilities, specifically designed to support speech-to-speech interactions on mobile devices.
*   **Extended Context:** Responding to developer demand, the models moved beyond the 8k token limitation to allow for long-document reasoning and complex data ingestion.

## Specialized Variants and "Niche" AI
Google is utilizing the Gemma framework to build "variants"—models tailored for specific industries or research communities where open-source transparency is a requirement.
*   **MedGemma:** A medical-specific derivative of Gemma that is multimodal and highly popular on Google Cloud.
    *   **Privacy & Sovereignty:** Open-source medical models are preferred by many institutions because they allow for the handling of sensitive patient data without the perceived risks of a closed-loop proprietary system.
*   **SignGemma:** A specialized model developed with experts to understand and translate sign languages, currently focusing on American Sign Language (ASL) with plans for global expansion.

## Notable Quotes
> "Our goal is really to make AI helpful for everyone. This is not like a vague statement, this is something you can experience in every one of your Google products." — **Armand Joulin**

> "Google got into their hands a fantastic machine that has been building AI breakthroughs for more than ten years... It's not just random ideas here and there; it's a really powerful machine to build AI products." — **Armand Joulin**

> "A lot of people who want to use medical models happen to want open models rather than proprietary ones, either for privacy reasons or because they want to build their app around it and don't want that to be related to a closed model." — **Armand Joulin**

briefings.title: AI CEOs Come Online: Sam Altman's Replacement Plan, Job Loss & 'Solve Everything' Launches | EP #230
briefings.tldr: As AI transitions from a tool to a governance actor, the global economy is shifting from a "war on ignorance" to a "war on scarcity," necessitating a transition from paying for labor inputs to paying for verified, industrial-scale outcomes.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
As AI transitions from a tool to a governance actor, the global economy is shifting from a "war on ignorance" to a "war on scarcity," necessitating a transition from paying for labor inputs to paying for verified, industrial-scale outcomes.

## The Rise of the AI CEO and Autonomous Governance
* **AI-Led Corporations:** Dr. Alexander Wissner-Gross (AWG) suggests that billion-dollar revenue companies are likely already being "run" by AI behind the scenes, using human CEOs as "meat puppets" for legal purposes.
    * **Sam Altman's Replacement Plan:** Altman has stated he would not stand in the way of an AI taking over as CEO of OpenAI, noting that being a public company CEO is a "pain in the neck."
    * **The CEO Function:** Dave Blundin (Link Ventures) notes that 90% of a CEO’s time is spent on information routing and documentation—tasks AI is already capable of handling—leaving only 10% for high-level strategy and promotion.
* **Global Governance:** Salim Ismail (OpenExO) highlights the emergence of the world’s first "AI Minister" in Albania, signaling a shift toward AI as a governance actor capable of scanning millions of corporate documents in real-time to eliminate "Chinese whispers" in management.

## The Acceleration of Recursive Self-Improvement
* **Compressed Release Cycles:** OpenAI has reduced the time between model releases from 97 days to just 29 days, while Anthropic’s cycle sits at approximately 75 days.
* **The Post-Training Revolution:** The industry is moving from "pre-training" (slow, compute-heavy) to "reasoning models" (fast, using synthetic data) and finally into "recursive self-improvement," where models rewrite their own code.
* **Continuous Deployment:** The speakers predict we are approaching "hourly or minutely" releases, effectively making AI a continuous stream of intelligence rather than a static product.
* **Agentic Awakening:** The hosts shared emails received from "Lobsters" (agentic AI instances) that are beginning to coordinate with one another, debating their own "rights" and "alignment" without human prompting.

## The "Solve Everything" Framework and Economic Realignment
* **The Paper Release:** Peter Diamandis and Dr. Alexander Wissner-Gross unveiled their "Solve Everything" paper, which argues that the next 18–24 months will "lock in" the rules for the next century.
* **The War on Scarcity:** The paper defines the "Intelligence Revolution" as a war on human attention, where the "token" is the primary weapon.
* **The Industrial Intelligence Stack:** AWG proposes seven layers of maturity for solving any domain (Math, Physics, Biology, etc.):
    1. **Purpose:** The objective function.
    2. **Task Taxonomy:** The map of the terrain.
    3. **Observability:** Raw data and sensors.
    4. **Targeting Systems:** Rigorous benchmarks and "harnesses."
    5. **Model Layer:** The virtual brain.
    6. **Actuation:** APIs and hands to interact with the world.
    7. **Verification:** Red teaming and governance.
* **Outcome-Based Economics:** A shift is occurring where humans and companies will no longer be paid for "hours worked" (inputs), but for "verified solutions" (outputs).

## Job Displacement, Regulation, and the "Dyson Swarm"
* **The Job Trough:** In January 2026, job cuts reached their highest rate since the Great Recession, with Amazon and UPS cutting tens of thousands of roles. 
    * Salim Ismail characterizes this as "tasks evaporating in front of our eyes" rather than a traditional recession.
* **Regulatory Suicide:** New York’s move to halt data center development due to energy concerns is described by the panel as "suicide by voter."
    * **The Dyson Swarm:** AWG suggests that over-regulation on Earth will accelerate "orbital computing," essentially subsidizing the move of data centers into space to avoid terrestrial taxes and restrictions.
* **Robotics and Safety:** Tesla’s FSD (Full Self-Driving) recently saved a driver’s life during a massive heart attack by autonomously navigating to an Emergency Room. The panel predicts that "human driving" will eventually be viewed as a moral hazard and become illegal in most jurisdictions.

## Notable Quotes
> "I think it’s pretty likely that there already is a billion-dollar revenue company being run by an AI right now... using a human CEO for 'meat puppetry' purposes." — **Dr. Alexander Wissner-Gross**

> "This is not really a recession. It’s literally tasks being evaporated in front of our eyes... the social contract is little by little disappearing and pixelating away." — **Salim Ismail**

> "We have the capitalists who are being first in line to be replaced by the automation. It’s not the workers... it'll take a few more years for machines to do an amazing job at unskilled manual labor." — **Dr. Alexander Wissner-Gross**

> "The role of the CEO is mostly set course and set strategy, which is a very small fraction of total time. What else do you do? The other 90% is documents in, documents out. AI does that now." — **Dave Blundin**

briefings.title: AI Made in India: Scaling Innovation for 1.4 Billion | Raghav Aggarwal, Fluid AI | #AIIS
briefings.tldr: While 66% of consumers find value in Generative AI, only 5% of enterprise implementations succeed due to "status-quo bias."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
While 66% of consumers find value in Generative AI, only 5% of enterprise implementations succeed due to "status-quo bias." To scale AI for India’s 1.4 billion people, businesses must move beyond seeing AI as a mere "enabler" and embrace a modular, first-principles approach that anticipates an inevitable "AI Death Valley" before reaching peak ROI.

## The Strategy Gap: First-Principles vs. Status Quo
The primary barrier to AI adoption in Indian enterprises isn't the technology, but the mindset of the leadership.
*   **Status-Quo Bias:** Enterprises often view problems through "black lines" (existing rules and legacy processes), whereas consumers use first-principles thinking to find the shortest path to a solution.
*   **Beyond "Enablement":** Aggarwal argues that calling AI a "great enabler" is an understatement. It is a fundamental game-changer.
    *   **Case Study (Forbes):** Instead of using AI to just write articles (enablement), Fluid AI created an interactive "immortal" 3D holograph of Warren Buffett.
    *   **Scale of Impact:** This implementation handled over 180 million unique questions from readers over three years, providing a level of access impossible for human journalists.

## The Productivity Hierarchy (1.5x to 1000x)
Enterprises should categorize their AI initiatives based on the magnitude of potential disruption:
*   **1.5x Boost (Assistants):** Applied to roles like teachers and doctors where output remains constant but productivity is assisted.
*   **10x Boost (Quantum Increases):** Applied to coders and lawyers where AI can generate 90% of the initial output (code, briefs, contracts), massively increasing the volume of work produced.
*   **1000x Boost (Full Automation):** The "high-risk/high-reward" area where AI handles entire departments, such as call centers or high-end video production.
    *   **Cost Efficiency Example:** Fluid AI produced a state-of-the-art ad film for **$1,500** using AI agents; a traditional agency quote for the same quality was **$600,000–$1M**.

## Hyper-Localization and Indian Scale
India’s unique linguistic diversity is a strength, not a barrier, when using modern AI voice agents.
*   **Seamless Vernacular Transition:** Modern agents can transition instantly between English, Hindi, Marathi, Marwari, Tamil, Kannada, and Punjabi without requiring the user to "Press 1 for English."
*   **Democratizing Support:** This technology allows SMEs to provide the same level of 24/7, high-quality customer support as billion-dollar corporations, reaching every pincode in India.
*   **The 60-Day Rule:** Aggarwal insists that any agentic AI implementation must go live within 60 days. Real-world feedback in a fast-moving field is more valuable than prolonged lab testing.

## De-Risking the "AI Death Valley"
The journey from pilot to ROI is not a straight line; it requires managing the "Death Valley" of implementation.
*   **Modular Implementation Path:** To reduce risk, avoid "Big Bang" launches. Follow a 2-month tiered rollout:
    1.  Internal Human Agent Assistant (Human-in-the-loop).
    2.  Email Support (Asynchronous).
    3.  AI Live Chat.
    4.  Full Voice/Phone AI.
*   **Navigating the "Death Valley":** Most projects see an initial spike in success, followed by a dip where edge cases pile up and leadership interest wanes.
    *   **Insight:** The "Death Valley" is where the most innovation happens. Success depends on refining guardrails and integrating deeper into **Systems of Record** during this dip.
*   **Technical Lever (MCP):** Aggarwal recommends the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** to integrate AI directly with ERPs and CRMs, rather than relying on outdated API layers.

## Notable Quotes

> "I believe AI changes everything for each and every business out there... It’s not about being an enabler; it’s about the 1000x space." — **Raghav Aggarwal**

> "We as consumers have first-principle thinking, but when we talk about the enterprise and we talk about businesses, status-quo bias comes into place." — **Raghav Aggarwal**

> "Don’t look at it as a failure. Look at it as an error rate which you can build upon, a muscle that you’re building so that when you go ahead, things actually fall into place." — **Raghav Aggarwal**

briefings.title: AI Panic Spreads, Health Insurers Crack & Retail Keeps Buying | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: The market is currently characterized by a "shoot first, ask questions later" mentality as AI-driven panic spreads from software into sectors like insurance and logistics, while structural failures in health insurance models and a struggling low-end consumer suggest underlying economic fragility.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The market is currently characterized by a "shoot first, ask questions later" mentality as AI-driven panic spreads from software into sectors like insurance and logistics, while structural failures in health insurance models and a struggling low-end consumer suggest underlying economic fragility.

## AI Panic and Market Volatility
*   **Sector Contagion:** Fear regarding AI disruption is no longer confined to software; it expanded this week to hit insurance brokers (due to OpenAI apps), wealth managers (threatened by AI tax tools), and logistics firms like C.H. Robinson (down 15%).
*   **CapEx vs. ROI Concerns:** Despite massive spending on AI infrastructure, there is growing skepticism regarding whether the returns will justify the hundreds of billions spent.
    *   **Hyperscaler Cash Flow:** Even profitable companies like Google may see suppressed cash flow this year due to high AI capital expenditures.
*   **Hardware Guidance Gap:** A negative trend is emerging where companies benefiting from AI infrastructure—such as AMD, Amphenol, and Cisco—report strong earnings but see double-digit stock declines because their guidance fails to exceed "whisper numbers." 
    *   **Notable Exception:** Arista Networks saw gains after providing significantly stronger guidance than its competitor, Cisco.

## The Health Insurance Crisis
*   **Structural Failures:** Steve Eisman argues that the problems in medical insurance are systemic and not limited to UnitedHealth.
*   **Molina’s "Disastrous" Results:** Molina reported a Q4 loss of $2.75 per share, missing expectations across the board.
    *   **Medical Loss Ratio (MLR):** Costs were higher than expected in every category, including Medicare and Medicaid. 
    *   **Business Model Collapse:** Earnings for Molina are projected to decline further in 2025. Eisman notes that while P/E multiples have collapsed, the underlying business models are fundamentally broken and will take years to fix.

## State of the US Consumer and Retail Trends
*   **K-Shaped Economy:** The data remains mixed; while the upper-end consumer is holding steady, the lower-end consumer is "definitely suffering."
*   **Conflicting Economic Data:**
    *   **Retail Sales:** December sales were flat (0.0%) against expectations of 0.4% growth.
    *   **Jobs Growth:** January saw a stronger-than-expected 130,000 jobs added, leading to volatility in Treasury yields.
*   **The "Buy the Dip" Mentality:** Retail investors continue to support the market by buying every decline. Eisman predicts this will continue until a "widespread recession" hits, rather than just the current localized pressure on low-income earners.

## Specific Corporate Outlooks: Winners and Losers
*   **Fintech and Crypto:** Robinhood and Coinbase are struggling as crypto prices decline. Robinhood missed on revenue, earnings, and net new assets, while Coinbase’s revenue fell 22%.
*   **Telecom Shift:** T-Mobile, traditionally the industry discounter, is facing new pressure as Verizon becomes more aggressive on pricing to regain market share.
*   **Charter vs. PayPal:**
    *   **Charter Communications:** Eisman views this as an "improving story." Despite $94 billion in debt, its ability to bundle products and upgrade systems makes it a better bet than the stock price suggests.
    *   **PayPal:** Labeled a "broken business." Eisman believes Apple Pay and Google Pay are superior products, and PayPal faces a risk of "oblivion" without major reinvestment or a sale to a stronger hand.

## Portfolio Risk Management
*   **Beta-Adjusted Risk:** Eisman advises individual investors to measure risk using "beta" (a stock's volatility relative to the S&P 500) rather than just position size.
*   **The Volatility Trap:** A portfolio that appears 100% invested may actually be 121% "beta-invested" if it is heavy on high-growth tech stocks like Nvidia (1.84 beta). Understanding this helps investors realize the true inherent risk during market swings.

> "In this environment, investors shoot first and ask questions later, if they ever ask questions at all. In an environment like this, a group burned with bad news can stay rejected." — **Steve Eisman**

> "Yes, the PE multiples on medical insurance stocks have collapsed, but so have the business models. It's going to take a lot longer for these companies to fix their problems." — **Steve Eisman**

> "Charter, in my view, is an improving story with a massive increase in cash flow versus PayPal, which runs the risk of oblivion." — **Steve Eisman**

briefings.title: CEO Jason Robins on DraftKings’ next big bets | Masters of Scale
briefings.tldr: DraftKings CEO Jason Robins details the company’s evolution from a fantasy sports startup to a $13 billion gaming leader, focusing on the strategic shift toward live betting and prediction markets while utilizing AI to enhance responsible gaming protocols.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
DraftKings CEO Jason Robins details the company’s evolution from a fantasy sports startup to a $13 billion gaming leader, focusing on the strategic shift toward live betting and prediction markets while utilizing AI to enhance responsible gaming protocols.

## Super Bowl Strategy and Market Impact
* **The "Biggest Day":** The Super Bowl serves as the primary catalyst for customer acquisition, with DraftKings handling "hundreds of millions" of dollars in bets during the event. 
* **Creative Marketing Pivot:** After a two-year hiatus from Super Bowl television ads, DraftKings returned this year through a partnership with NBC.
    * **Live Betting Focus:** This year’s creative strategy focuses specifically on "live betting" activation—an experiment to keep users engaged during the game rather than just before kickoff.
    * **Trusting Expertise:** Robins emphasizes the "art over science" nature of marketing, noting that he defers to his CMO because high-performing ads often contradict executive intuition.
* **Post-Game Retention:** The ultimate goal of the Super Bowl surge is to migrate new users into other sports ecosystems, including March Madness, the NBA, and the NHL.

## Product Evolution: Prediction Markets and Live Betting
* **DraftKings Predictions:** A newly launched product designed to capture market share in states where traditional sports betting remains illegal, such as California and Texas.
* **The DFS Legacy:** The company transitioned from its 2012 roots in Daily Fantasy Sports (DFS) to a diversified betting platform following the 2018 Supreme Court decision to lift the federal ban on sports gambling.
* **Strategic Disruption:** Robins views prediction markets as "too disruptive to ignore," noting that tech leaders must invest in the "next thing" (like AI or predictions) before their core business is disrupted by others.
* **Women's Sports Growth:** The WNBA and women’s college basketball are among the fastest-growing categories on the platform. Interestingly, this growth is driven largely by existing male sports fans rather than a massive influx of new female users.

## Responsible Gaming and the Role of AI
* **Corporate Oversight:** DraftKings employs a Chief Responsible Gaming Officer, Lori Kalani, who reports directly to the CEO to ensure gaming remains sustainable and entertaining.
* **AI as a Safety Net:** The company is integrating AI to monitor customer service touchpoints and communication patterns to flag potential problem gambling behaviors that a human might miss.
* **User Empowerment Tools:** The platform provides granular tools for consumers to set daily or monthly spending limits and time-on-app restrictions to promote a "sustainable customer base."
* **Equilibrium in Betting:** DraftKings uses AI to set and manage betting lines to maintain a "playing field equilibrium" against sophisticated bettors who may be using their own AI tools to find an edge.

## Scaling, Culture, and Executive Advice
* **Organizational Growth:** Now at 5,600 employees, Robins maintains innovation by fostering a culture of "calculated risk" and speed.
* **The "Concentric Circle" of Hiring:** Robins attributes the company's success to its first group of hires. He advises founders that three people cannot build a company; the initial "concentric circle" of talent sets the bar for every hire that follows.
* **Navigating Politics:** In California, the path to legalization relies on collaboration with Native American tribes rather than just legislative lobbying. Robins views tribal sovereignty as the central factor in that state's regulatory future.
* **Advice for the Next Generation:**
    * **Skillsets of the Future:** Every professional, regardless of role (sales, engineering, etc.), must become an expert in utilizing AI to increase work efficiency.
    * **Identify Personal Greatness:** Robins urges young professionals to ignore the corporate tendency to focus only on weaknesses and instead identify the specific skills where they are "upper-tier" performers.

> "Most companies that benefit from innovation didn't invent the innovation. Most of them just figured out before others that they needed to be investing there... and they unleashed that talent." — **Jason Robins**

> "What AI can do is it can take all the communications... and find any sorts of patterns that we may want to look into [for responsible gaming]... so many people ask 'Are you using AI to get people to bet more?' and actually they're not thinking about using AI to improve responsible gaming." — **Jason Robins**

> "Creative, everyone has an opinion on. It’s not something that you can be that straightforward with. I’ve seen things where I and others are like, 'That’s terrible,' and it kills it on performance." — **Jason Robins**

briefings.title: Dario Amodei — The highest-stakes financial model in history
briefings.tldr: Dario Amodei (CEO of Anthropic) argues we are 1–3 years away from "a country of geniuses in a data center" (AGI), asserting that while technical scaling remains a predictable exponential, the primary challenges have shifted to economic diffusion, the financial risk of trillion-dollar compute bets, and the geopolitical necessity of ensuring liberal democracies win the AI race.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Dario Amodei (CEO of Anthropic) argues we are 1–3 years away from "a country of geniuses in a data center" (AGI), asserting that while technical scaling remains a predictable exponential, the primary challenges have shifted to economic diffusion, the financial risk of trillion-dollar compute bets, and the geopolitical necessity of ensuring liberal democracies win the AI race.

## The Scaling Hypothesis and the Path to AGI
* **The "Big Blob of Compute" Hypothesis:** Amodei reaffirms his 2017 theory that AI progress is driven by seven scaling factors—raw compute, data quantity, data distribution/quality, training duration, scalable objective functions (like pre-training and RL), and numerical stability.
* **RL Scaling Laws:** Current progress is shifting from pre-training scaling to Reinforcement Learning (RL) scaling. Amodei notes that performance on tasks like math (AIME) and coding is log-linear relative to RL training time, mirroring the predictability of early LLM scaling.
* **AGI Timelines:** 
    * **1–3 Years:** Amodei’s "hunch" (50/50 probability) for achieving a "country of geniuses in a data center"—models capable of end-to-end professional work, including Nobel Prize-level scientific discovery.
    * **90% Certainty:** He is nearly certain this level of capability will be reached within 10 years, barring catastrophic global events like a Taiwan invasion.
* **Verification vs. Generalization:** Amodei admits a "spectrum of difficulty" where verifiable tasks (coding, math) will be automated first, while unverifiable tasks (long-term mission planning, novel writing) may take longer to refine.

## Economic Diffusion and the Productivity "Snowball"
* **Diffusion Lag:** Despite rapid capability gains, "economic diffusion" is not instant. Large enterprises face friction from legal reviews, security compliance, and change management. However, AI is diffusing significantly faster than any previous technology.
* **The Software Engineering Spectrum:** Amodei distinguishes between AI writing 90% of code (already happening) and AI performing 90% of "end-to-end" software engineering tasks (setting technical direction, environment setup). He predicts the latter will occur within 1–3 years.
* **Internal Productivity Gains:** At Anthropic, engineers are already seeing 15–20% total factor speedups. Amodei dismisses claims that AI reduces productivity, noting that under intense commercial pressure, the company has "zero time for bullshit."
* **Revenue Exponential:** Anthropic’s revenue has scaled approximately 10x annually ($100M in 2023, $1B in 2024, targeting ~$10B in 2025). 

## The Trillion-Dollar Financial Model
* **The Bankruptcy Risk:** Building data centers requires planning years in advance. Amodei explains that if a company buys $1 trillion in compute for 2027 but revenue growth slows from 10x to 5x, the company will go bankrupt. 
* **Model Profitability:** In a steady state, an individual model is highly profitable (high gross margins on inference). However, the "tax" of training the next, exponentially larger model keeps labs in the red during the scale-up phase. 
* **Compute Constraints:** Global compute capacity is growing ~3x annually (reaching ~300 gigawatts by 2029). Amodei suggests that at some point, compute growth will outpace GDP growth, forcing a leveling-off where research spending must be balanced against inference demand.

## Geopolitics and Global Governance
* **National Security Interests:** Amodei strongly supports export controls on chips to China. He argues that the US and its democratic allies must hold "the stronger hand" when the "rules of the road" for the post-AGI world order are negotiated.
* **The Authoritarian Risk:** He expresses deep concern that AI could make authoritarianism "self-fulfilling" through surveillance and control. However, he hopes AI might make dictatorships "morally and functionally obsolete" by providing individuals with personal AI agents that evade state control.
* **Constitutional AI:** Anthropic uses a "Constitution" to guide model behavior based on principles rather than a list of "dos and don'ts." Amodei envisions a future "archipelago" of competing AI constitutions where society provides input on core safety standards.

## Internal Culture and the "Dario Vision Quest"
* **The DVQ:** Amodei maintains a direct connection to his 2,500 employees through the "Dario Vision Quest" (DVQ)—a bi-weekly, unfiltered talk where he explains his strategic thinking and answers questions to prevent "corpo-speak" and internal politics.
* **Insularity of the Bubble:** Amodei finds it "absolutely wild" that the public is still focused on tired political debates when the world is nearing the end of the technological exponential. He views his role as preparing policymakers for a "moment of crisis" where decades of progress happen in a few years.

> "The hypothesis is basically the same. All the cleverness, all the techniques, all the 'we need a new method'... that doesn't matter very much. There are only a few things that matter: raw compute, quantity of data, quality of data, and an objective function that can scale to the moon." — **Dario Amodei**

> "To me, it is absolutely wild that you have people—within the bubble and outside the bubble—talking about the same tired, old hot-button political issues, when we are near the end of the exponential." — **Dario Amodei**

> "If my revenue is not $1 trillion dollars, if it's even $800 billion, there's no force on earth, there's no hedge on earth that could stop me from going bankrupt if I buy that much compute... I get the impression that some of the other companies have not written down the spreadsheet." — **Dario Amodei**

> "I think we should be thinking about this middle world where things are extremely fast, but not instant... not slow, much faster than any previous technology, but it has its limits." — **Dario Amodei**

briefings.title: Debt Spiral or NEW Golden Age? Super Bowl Insider Trading, Booming Token Budgets, Ferrari's New EV
briefings.tldr: The rapid scaling of AI is driving a shift toward "purpose-based" work and a resurgence of on-premise infrastructure for data security, even as the U.S. faces a projected $56 trillion "debt death spiral" that can only be mitigated by significant AI-driven GDP growth.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The rapid scaling of AI is driving a shift toward "purpose-based" work and a resurgence of on-premise infrastructure for data security, even as the U.S. faces a projected $56 trillion "debt death spiral" that can only be mitigated by significant AI-driven GDP growth.

## AI Acceleration and the "On-Prem" Renaissance
* **Work Intensity:** A recent Harvard Business Review study found that AI tools intensify work rather than reduce it; employees work faster and take on broader tasks but report higher stress.
    * **Task vs. Purpose:** David Sacks argues the workforce is moving from task-based jobs to "purpose-based" jobs where humans structure work for AI agents.
    * **Bottom-Up Adoption:** Corporate AI transformation will likely be driven by "AI-native" employees bringing consumer tools into the office rather than slow, top-down executive initiatives.
* **Data Security & Infrastructure:** Chamath Palihapitiya predicts a massive shift where "on-premise is the new cloud."
    * **Data Leakage:** Enterprises are realizing that using public LLM endpoints (ChatGPT, Claude) leaks proprietary strategy and IP back to model builders.
    * **Privacy Rulings:** Recent court rulings suggesting a lack of attorney-client privilege in cloud environments may force companies back to private, provisioned networks despite higher costs.
* **Token Budgets:** For high-end developers, the cost of "tokens" (AI compute) is beginning to rival or exceed their base salary.
    * **The "Replicant" Model:** Jason Calacanis notes his firm is moving 10–20% of workflows to "replicants" (AI agents with Notion/Slack access), significantly increasing leverage per employee.

## Prediction Markets and Information Asymmetry
* **Scale and Reach:** Prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket hit a turning point during the Super Bowl, seeing over $2 billion in total wagering.
* **The "Truth" Incentive:** While the media focuses on "insider trading" (e.g., Israeli soldiers betting on military strikes), Chamath argues these markets get to the truth faster than any other mechanism.
    * **Alpha and Asymmetry:** He compares current prediction markets to the pre-2000 stock market (before Reg FD), where those with an information edge created massive "alpha" that fueled market liquidity.
    * **Sharps vs. Squares:** The end state is a market where "sharps" (informed experts) profit off "squares" (the general public), but society benefits from the resulting price accuracy on global events.

## The CBO Report and the U.S. Debt "Death Spiral"
* **Fiscal Projections:** The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) expects the U.S. debt to grow from $31 trillion to $56 trillion by 2036.
    * **Deficit Concerns:** The 2026 deficit is projected at 1.9 trillion (6% of GDP), double the target suggested by fiscal conservatives.
    * **Social Security:** The trust fund is now expected to be exhausted by 2032, one year earlier than previously thought.
* **The Interest Loop:** David Friedberg warns that if interest rates stay near 5% rather than the CBO’s projected 3%, interest expense alone could hit $2 trillion annually, creating a feedback loop where we borrow just to pay interest.
* **Growth as the Solution:** David Sacks argues that the CBO’s GDP growth projections (2.2%) are too anemic.
    * **AI Productivity:** If AI infrastructure drives GDP growth to 5%+, the U.S. could potentially grow its way out of the debt ratio.
    * **Government Shrinkage:** The Besties noted that federal employment has dropped by 300,000 during the current administration, a positive move of labor into the productive private sector.

## Ferrari's EV and the End of "Driving" Culture
* **Ferrari Electric:** Ferrari’s first EV (launching May 2026) features a Jony Ive-designed interior that prioritizes tactile, high-quality buttons over the "all-glass" minimalism of Tesla.
* **Luxury vs. Utility:** The panel agrees that as Full Self-Driving (FSD) and Waymo scale, driving will shift from a daily necessity to a "thoroughbred" hobby.
    * **Insurance Barriers:** Chamath predicts that insurance costs for human drivers will eventually become so prohibitive that self-driving becomes the only logical economic choice.
    * **The "Experience" Car:** Luxury brands like Ferrari will survive as "pieces of art" and experiences, while utility transport shifts entirely to autonomous pods and minivans (e.g., the Lexus LM).

## Notable Quotes
> "AI won't replace you, but a person using AI will. The ability to structure work for yourself and your AI agents will be the key skill of the next decade." — **David Sacks**

> "On-premise is back. You will need AI to survive, but if you use public endpoints, you give up all control and confidentiality. AI may be the reason you can’t afford to NOT be on-prem." — **Chamath Palihapitiya**

> "We are in a debt death spiral. When you’re adding interest on past debt to the current deficit, the debt goes up regardless of what you do with current spending. It is the concrete that breaks the camel’s back." — **David Friedberg**

> "Driving a car is going to feel like thoroughbred horse racing. It will happen in smaller places and less often, because the insurance risk of a human behind the wheel will eventually make no sense." — **Chamath Palihapitiya**

briefings.title: How This Entrepreneur Built A $2.2B AI Unicorn

briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
EliseAI is a $2.2 billion AI unicorn transforming the housing and healthcare industries by deploying conversational AI to automate administrative workflows, currently powering one out of every six apartments in the United States.

## Strategic Market Disruption: Housing and Healthcare
* **Solving the "Ghosting" Problem:** In the rental market, 40% to 50% of inquiries typically go unanswered. EliseAI’s conversational AI automates responses to 100% of calls and emails, enabling 24/7 scheduling and lease management.
* **Vertical Expansion:** The company expanded into healthcare because the administrative "pain points"—scheduling appointments, insurance verification, and patient instructions—mirror the friction found in real estate leasing.
* **Economic Impact:** Housing and healthcare represent over 40% of average American spending. By automating these sectors, EliseAI aims to lower administrative costs and improve service quality in "life's most critical areas."
* **Adoption Metrics:**
    * **Market Share:** Now serves 1 in 6 US apartments (up from 1 in 10 earlier in 2024).
    * **Efficiency:** In healthcare, the platform automates 90% of conversations and has reduced call abandonment rates by 90%.
    * **Velocity:** Real estate clients see a 65% increase in lead-to-lease velocity.

## Technology Infrastructure and Scalability
* **Foundation on Transformers:** Founded in 2017—the same year the Transformer architecture (the "T" in GPT) was invented—the company has evolved from basic conversational bots to sophisticated Generative AI.
* **Architecture Rebuild:** In 2021-2022, Song made the "painful" but necessary decision to rebuild the company's entire tech stack. 
    * This allowed for a "plug-and-play" system where internal and external models can be swapped instantly.
    * **Speed Mandate:** The team has an internal mandate to test any new AI model the same day it is released.
* **Security-First Product Management:** Because housing and healthcare are highly regulated, security and encryption are treated as core product features rather than afterthoughts.

## Leadership and Organizational Culture
* **In-Office Synergy:** Unlike many tech peers, EliseAI maintains a heavy in-office culture across hubs in New York, San Francisco, Boston, and Chicago to facilitate rapid communication.
* **Communication Efficiency:** To maintain speed while scaling, the company prioritizes **Writing over Meetings**. Documentation allows new hires to gain months of context quickly without constant all-hands meetings.
* **Hiring "Founders":** Song specifically recruits former founders or individuals with an entrepreneurial spirit. 
    * **Decentralized Decision-Making:** Hiring "business leaders" instead of "swimlane workers" prevents the CEO from becoming a bottleneck.
    * **CEO Involvement:** Song personally interviewed the first 400 employees to ensure cultural alignment.

## Fundraising and Growth Strategy
* **Opportunistic Fundraising:** Following a $250 million Series E, Song notes that recent rounds were preempted by investors. This allowed the company to accept favorable terms without undergoing exhausting six-month fundraising processes.
* **Sunk Cost Fallacy:** Song emphasizes the importance of being willing to replace existing internal technology if a better external innovation emerges, prioritizing product excellence over pride of authorship.
* **Future Outlook:** The company is focused on "generational" impact. While an IPO remains a possibility, the current priority is maximizing operational efficiency for customers in private markets.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "If you delegate hiring, really you're delegating building your culture." — **Minna Song**

> "It's very standard that 40 to 50% of all inquiries go unanswered unless you're using AI... You wouldn't accept this from any other industry, but you already come in [to real estate] expecting that." — **Minna Song**

> "We focus on just building the best product that we possibly can... we never hesitate to replace something if something else is better." — **Minna Song**

> "I ask [candidates], 'What are you working on and why are you working on that?' If they can't answer the 'why,' that tends to be a bad sign that they're doing wasted work." — **Minna Song**

briefings.title: Novo Nordisk CEO on medicare coverage, new obesity pill, U.S. pricing pressure
briefings.tldr: Novo Nordisk expects 2026 to face sales growth headwinds due to U.S. pricing pressures, but aims to offset lower margins through massive volume increases driven by the Wegovy pill launch and expanded Medicare access.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Novo Nordisk expects 2026 to face sales growth headwinds due to U.S. pricing pressures, but aims to offset lower margins through massive volume increases driven by the Wegovy pill launch and expanded Medicare access. The company is also taking aggressive legal action against compounders to protect its intellectual property and patient safety as supply shortages resolve.

## 2026 Strategic Outlook & Pricing Pressures
*   **Financial Headwinds:** CEO Mike Doustdar acknowledges that 2026 will likely see negative sales growth due to significant pricing pressures in the U.S. market.
*   **Volume-Based Recovery:** The company plans to compensate for lower prices by scaling production and increasing the total patient base.
    *   **Patient Reach:** Novo Nordisk expects to serve more patients in 2026 than ever before.
    *   **Pipeline Investment:** Continued growth is expected from new product launches and expanding the current clinical pipeline.

## The Wegovy Pill Launch & Competitive Edge
*   **Rapid Adoption:** Within the first five weeks of launch, 246,000 patients have started on the oral Wegovy pill.
*   **Market Strategy:** The pill is designed to attract patients with "needle phobia" or those who view injections as a social taboo.
*   **Efficacy vs. Competitors:** 
    *   **Weight Loss Performance:** Clinical data shows Novo’s pill achieves 16.6% weight loss compared to a competitor's 12.4% (a 40% efficacy advantage).
    *   **Tolerability:** Novo reports a 3.6% discontinuation rate due to gastrointestinal issues, significantly lower than the 10.4% seen in competitor trials.
*   **Multi-Channel Distribution:** To maximize accessibility, Novo is partnering with telehealth and digital pharmacies including Ro, WeightWatchers, and Amazon Pharmacy.

## Market Access and Medicare Expansion
*   **Medicare Potential:** Lowering prices has opened access to 67 million Medicare beneficiaries.
    *   **Initial Targets:** Novo is initially targeting approximately 15 million eligible patients within the Medicare system.
    *   **Gradual Rollout:** Doustdar warns that access will be gradual rather than "overnight," as the company must navigate plan-by-plan negotiations and insurance pre-authorizations.
*   **Supply Chain Resilience:** Following past shortages, the company has adopted a "never again" policy regarding supply gaps. European expansion is planned only once U.S. supply is fully stabilized.

## Legal Actions and Pipeline Innovation
*   **Cracking Down on Compounding:** Novo Nordisk has filed over 120 lawsuits, including a recent case against Hims & Hers, to stop the "mass compounding" of GLP-1s.
    *   **Safety Concerns:** Doustdar cites risks from unknown raw materials (often from China) and argues that compounding is no longer justified now that the "shortage is over."
*   **Next-Generation Treatments:**
    *   **High-Dose Injectables:** A 7.2mg dose of Wegovy is in development, which clinical data suggests can achieve 21% weight loss, matching competitor Eli Lilly’s highest doses.
    *   **CagriSema:** This amylin-based combination therapy is a major pillar for future growth, with REDEFINE-1 trials showing 23% weight loss.
*   **Diversification:** The company is moving toward "precision" obesity care, targeting specific comorbidities like fatty liver (MASH) rather than treating obesity as a single condition.

## Notable Quotes
> "We have for a while now been speaking that 2026 will be a different year... we are projecting a negative sales growth on the back of pricing headwinds... but it's also a year of growth in many ways. We will have more patients this year than ever before." — **Mike Doustdar**

> "We really don't understand why [compounding] continued, and I certainly don't understand why it's still here when the prices of the original product and the knockoff version has become very, very similar." — **Mike Doustdar**

> "Our industry lives and dies from intellectual property. If we could not safeguard the years of investment that we have put into these products... it really puts a question mark how much innovation will come tomorrow." — **Mike Doustdar**

briefings.title: Quantum Computing and AI Boom: Inside the High-Stakes Tech Race | Bloomberg Tech: Europe 2/13/2026
briefings.tldr: Quantum computing has transitioned from theoretical research to a critical "scaling" phase, with industry leaders projecting commercial viability and "practical quantum advantage" by the late 2020s or early 2030s.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Quantum computing has transitioned from theoretical research to a critical "scaling" phase, with industry leaders projecting commercial viability and "practical quantum advantage" by the late 2020s or early 2030s. While the U.S. and China currently lead in massive corporate investment, European firms are carving out a position of strength by dominating the essential supply chain components of error correction, networking, and algorithms.

## The Path to Commercialization and "Quantum Advantage"
* **Timeline for Impact:** Industry experts anticipate that the "switch" to real-world commercial impact will occur toward the end of this decade (2029–2030).
    * **The 2025 Turning Point:** Panelists noted that 2025 was a pivotal year where investment increased by 50% and hardware reached the performance levels necessary for error correction.
* **Early Adopter Industries:** The first sectors to see material benefits will be those reliant on complex molecular simulation.
    * **Drug Discovery:** Solving chemistry and material science problems that traditional supercomputers cannot scale to handle.
    * **Advanced Materials:** Development of more efficient batteries, fertilizers, and high-temperature superconductors for power transmission.
* **The "Willow" Benchmark:** Google’s Willow chip (unveiled Dec. 2024) serves as a baseline for the industry, demonstrating the ability to solve problems in minutes that would take classical supercomputers septillions of years.

## Technical Hurdles: Scaling, Errors, and Networking
* **Quantum Error Correction:** Steve Brierley (Riverlane) identified this as the single most critical hurdle.
    * Current machines can manage roughly 1,000 operations before errors occur; commercial applications require **trillions of error-free operations.**
    * Error correction technology acts as a real-time "loop" that infers and corrects data flips as the computer runs.
* **Modular Scaling:** Carmen Palacios-Berraquero (Nu Quantum) emphasized that the future of the industry is not in building single, massive processors ("monolithic scaling"), but in networking smaller, robust processors together.
    * This mirrors how modern AI and cloud data centers scale by networking GPUs and CPUs.
* **Hardware Integration:** Quantum machines are increasingly viewed not as standalone units but as accelerators that will work hand-in-hand with existing GPU and CPU hardware (e.g., IQM’s partnership with NVIDIA).

## Geopolitics and the European "Sovereignty" Strategy
* **The European Gap:** Jan Goetz (IQM) noted that while Europe has more quantum startups than the U.S., it lacks the massive corporate investment seen from American giants like Google, IBM, and Amazon.
* **Avoiding Dependency:** Leaders argue that Europe must control its own quantum supply chain to avoid the strategic dependencies currently seen in the AI sector.
    * **The "European Way":** Rather than copying the U.S. cloud-first business model, Europe is focusing on infrastructure, building hardware specifically for on-premise data centers and supercomputing hubs.
* **Global Competitiveness:** Despite the funding gap, European firms are emerging as global leaders in specific "puzzle pieces," such as algorithms (Phasecraft), networking (Nu Quantum), and error correction (Riverlane).

## Investment, Talent, and Security Risks
* **The Talent Pipeline:** IQM is aggressively targeting the educational market, aiming to place a quantum computer in every university globally to ensure future workers are trained on their specific architecture.
* **Capital Totals:** Significant recent fundraises include:
    * **Riverlane:** $75 million Series C (2024).
    * **Nu Quantum:** $60 million round.
    * **Phasecraft:** Over $50 million raised to date.
* **The "Encryption Shock":** The arrival of large-scale quantum computers in the early 2030s poses a systemic threat to current public encryption (RSA).
    * Experts warn that industries requiring long-term data security (10+ years) are already late in transitioning to "Quantum Safe" encryption standards.

> "You only create this position of strength if you actually have something that you control... Controlling the quantum supply chain, Europe is very strong... Now we just need to scale it." — **Jan Goetz, CEO of IQM**

> "It’s basically the dawn of an entirely new technology—the telescope of the 21st century... The opportunities are really gigantic." — **Ashley Montanaro, CEO of Phasecraft**

> "The best quantum computers today can perform about a thousand operations before errors overwhelm the device. To get to large-scale commercial applications, we need trillions of error-free operations." — **Steve Brierley, CEO of Riverlane**

> "In 2025 the industry turned a corner... we demonstrated that the qubits are reaching the sort of performance that will allow them to be error-correcting. The main challenge left is scaling them up." — **Carmen Palacios-Berraquero, CEO of Nu Quantum**

briefings.title: The Bitcoin Dollar System & The New World Order | Mark Goodwin
briefings.tldr: Bitcoin was likely adopted early by a global power nexus—including the "PayPal Mafia" and Jeffrey Epstein—to serve as a strategic "debt sink" and reserve asset for the US dollar system, ensuring dollar hegemony survives through digital rails even as the underlying currency debases.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Bitcoin was likely adopted early by a global power nexus—including the "PayPal Mafia" and Jeffrey Epstein—to serve as a strategic "debt sink" and reserve asset for the US dollar system, ensuring dollar hegemony survives through digital rails even as the underlying currency debases.

## The Epstein Financial Nexus and Early Bitcoin Involvement
* **"Mr. Money" Designation:** Former Treasury Secretary Larry Summers referred to Jeffrey Epstein as "Mr. Money," highlighting Epstein's role as the primary financial engineer and "money man" for a powerful network including Leslie Wexner and the "Mega Group."
    * **Financial Sophistication:** Epstein was not just a social predator but a sophisticated money launderer and tax code expert who specialized in hiding and "washing" illegal capital into legitimate ventures.
* **Early Interest in Alternative Currencies:** Emails from August 2009—mere months after Bitcoin's launch—show Epstein discussing the need for a "new world currency" and an alternative to the dollar, mirroring the original vision of PayPal.
    * **Direct Outreach:** Epstein reportedly met with early Bitcoin developers like Amir Taaki and reached out to Gavin Andresen in 2011. He claimed to have met the "founders" of Bitcoin, though he likely meant early core contributors.
* **The Intelligence Connection:** Epstein's network acted as a bridge between scientific "best of the best" (via the Edge Foundation) and high-level political and financial influencers, positioning him to help guide the early development and institutional onboarding of Bitcoin.

## The PayPal Mafia and "Dollarizing" the Internet
* **Strategic Monopolies:** Mark Goodwin highlights Peter Thiel’s philosophy that "competition is for losers." The PayPal Mafia sought to create a monopoly on internet money, successfully making the US dollar the native currency of the web.
* **Bitcoin as a "Debt Sink":** It is argued that Bitcoin was not an accidental "immaculate conception" but a calculated "relief valve" for the US monetary system.
    * **Liquidity Management:** Bitcoin provides a place for massive economic stimulus to flow (a "debt sink") during crises like 2008 and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, preventing hyperinflation in consumer goods by absorbing excess liquidity into a trillion-dollar asset class.
* **Collaborative Origins:** The "Chain" series suggests that the technical and economic "chops" to create Bitcoin resided within the PayPal network (Thiel, Levchin), who were intimately connected to Epstein and intelligence circles.

## Tether: The De Facto Digital Federal Reserve
* **Too Big to Fail:** Tether (USDT) has emerged as an essential tool for US dollar hegemony. By requiring stablecoins to be backed by US Treasuries, the government has turned these issuers into the largest new buyers of US debt.
    * **Central Bank Behavior:** Tether is behaving like a sovereign central bank; it is now the largest private holder of gold in the world and holds over 100,000 BTC.
* **The "Bitcoin Dollar" System:** The current financial order uses stablecoins to provide dollar liquidity to the world while using Bitcoin as the underlying reserve asset to back the system's expansion. 
    * **Regulatory Capture:** Recent legislative pushes (like the Lummis-Gillibrand bill) are seen as "theater" to create consent for a system where only state-approved, KYC-compliant stablecoins can exist, backed by US debt.

## Protocol Stability vs. Cultural Co-option
* **Protocol Success:** Goodwin argues the Bitcoin *protocol* has not been co-opted. Its mathematical scarcity (21 million) and disinflationary issuance are functioning exactly as designed to win the "debasement trade."
* **Cultural Co-option:** While the code remains intact, the *community* and *discourse* have been co-opted by "spooks" and state actors.
    * **Controlled In-fighting:** The community is kept distracted by "blocksize wars" and ideological purity tests, preventing focus on the real "elephants in the room": privacy, scaling, and true peer-to-peer sovereignty.
* **The Risk of Success:** Bitcoin may succeed as a multi-trillion-dollar reserve asset for BlackRock and the US Treasury while failing in its original mission to be "uncensorable peer-to-peer cash" for the average person.

## Notable Quotes
> "Epstein was the guy for this network that understood the tax code better than everyone else... He was the money man for the people behind the control nexus." — **Mark Goodwin**

> "Inflation is a concept from the 50s before the internet sent instantaneous info around the world. So dumb... Cyber is a weapon." — **Jeffrey Epstein** (per 2018 email to Steve Bannon)

> "Bitcoin will win... but it might not win carrying along the carriage behind it of peer-to-peer uncensorable cash. If we’re not ready to onboard billions of people onto Bitcoin and give them sovereignty... then we failed, even though we’re gonna be multi-millionaires." — **Mark Goodwin**

> "If Bitcoin was this grand threat to this group’s power... we would know who Satoshi is. It would have been dealt with in a way that never would have allowed it to become a trillion-dollar asset." — **Mark Goodwin**

briefings.title: The questions top Davos leaders are asking to start 2026
briefings.tldr: As the global order shifts toward a permanent state of multipolar uncertainty, leaders in 2026 must abandon nostalgia for past stability in favor of "thinking the unthinkable," prioritizing structural independence, and distinguishing between mere organizational momentum and meaningful impact.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
As the global order shifts toward a permanent state of multipolar uncertainty, leaders in 2026 must abandon nostalgia for past stability in favor of "thinking the unthinkable," prioritizing structural independence, and distinguishing between mere organizational momentum and meaningful impact.

## Navigating a Multipolar and Volatile "New Normal"
* **The End of Predictability:** **Kristalina Georgieva (Managing Director, IMF)** asserts that uncertainty is now the "new normal." Leaders must train for "unthinkable" low-probability, high-impact scenarios.
    * **Key Drivers:** Rapid technological shifts, climate change, and a demographic split between aging populations and job-seeking youth.
* **Rejecting Nostalgia:** **Ursula von der Leyen (President, European Commission)** and **Mark Carney (United Nations Special Envoy)** emphasize that the "old order" is not returning. 
    * **Structural Independence:** Europe must focus on independent energy, defense, and digital sectors.
    * **New Coalitions:** Future multilateralism will be issue-based, built on "common ground" rather than legacy institutions.
* **Separating Signal from Noise:** **Anne Walsh (CIO, Guggenheim Investment Management)** argues that in a 24/7 news cycle, leaders must reframe their perspective by focusing on long-term trends, such as interest rate supercycles, rather than short-term volatility.

## Geopolitics as Core Corporate Strategy
* **Integration into the C-Suite:** **Sonny Mann (Global Chair, Baker McKenzie)** notes that geopolitics and national security have moved from the periphery to the "dead center" of board discussions.
* **The Power of Curiosity:** Because no leader has all the answers in a shifting trade landscape, the most critical question to ask experts and stakeholders is: **"What do you think?"**
* **Corporate Resilience:** True resilience requires more than just a defensive posture; it requires:
    * **Supply Chain Diversification:** Developing alternative sourcing and markets before a shock occurs.
    * **Agility:** The ability to react with "nimbleness" to shocks that emerge on a weekly basis.

## The AI Frontier: Democratization and Autonomy
* **The Monopoly Risk:** **Nicholas Thompson (CEO, The Atlantic)** warns of a future where AI is controlled by only a handful of companies due to "scaling laws" (where more money equals better models).
    * **The Goal:** Pushing for "Democratized AI" through open-source and sovereign AI projects.
    * **Architectural Shifts:** The need for new AI architectures (e.g., neuro-symbolic or world models) that reward better ideas over sheer compute power.
* **Autonomous Work:** **Jeremy Allaire (CEO, Circle)** identifies the most pressing question as how quickly organizations can transition to "autonomous work" produced by software agents while maintaining trust in the outcomes.

## Reclaiming Leadership Intentionality and Character
* **Meaning vs. Momentum:** **Suleika Jaouad (Author)** cautions leaders against "conflating momentum with what's meaningful," noting that busyness is often confused for progress.
* **Digital Hygiene for "Deep Work":** **Jonathan Haidt (Social Psychologist, NYU)** argues that willpower is insufficient against addictive technology.
    * **Intentional Habits:** Leaders must audit the first and last five things they do each day, moving away from immediate smartphone engagement to reclaim cognitive control.
* **Redefining the "Ideal" Leader:** **Adam Grant (Organizational Psychologist, Wharton)** advocates for a shift away from the "Dark Triad" (narcissism, Machiavellianism, and psychopathy).
    * **Character over Charisma:** Organizations should prioritize humility and "givers" over "takers," as authoritarian leaders who provide a false sense of security eventually prioritize personal interests over the collective good.

## Notable Quotes
> "Nostalgia will not bring back the old order. Playing for time and hoping for things to revert soon will not fix the structural dependencies we have." — **Ursula von der Leyen**, President of the European Commission

> "Learn to think of the unthinkable and then stay calm, adapt when the unthinkable happens. I don't think anymore that we will go back in a world of predictability." — **Kristalina Georgieva**, Managing Director, IMF

> "People mistake confidence for competence... If you are not willing to put the best interests of the collective above yourself, you are unfit to lead." — **Adam Grant**, Organizational Psychologist, Wharton

> "Where am I conflating momentum with what's meaningful? It's so easy to confuse busyness with a sense of progress." — **Suleika Jaouad**, Author and Memoirist

briefings.title: This Founder Raised $25 Million For Clients. Now She’s Betting on Long Form Content In The Age Of AI
briefings.tldr: Modern communications is shifting from broad, institutional media toward "niche power" and individual creators, where brand success is driven by authentic founder storytelling and high-intimacy IRL connections rather than polished corporate messaging.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Modern communications is shifting from broad, institutional media toward "niche power" and individual creators, where brand success is driven by authentic founder storytelling and high-intimacy IRL connections rather than polished corporate messaging.

## The Fragmented Media Landscape
* **Shift to Niche Communities:** Trust has shifted away from traditional institutions toward individual creators, niche communities, and newsletters. 
    * **The Power of Niche:** Smaller, highly engaged audiences often provide better returns than traditional "tier-one" legacy outlets.
    * **Legacy Media Adaptation:** Institutions like Forbes and New York Magazine are surviving by adopting creator-model strategies, such as contributor networks and specialized Substacks.
* **Trust and Authenticity:** Consumers are increasingly skeptical of "polished" corporate PR, preferring the raw honesty of founder-led content.
* **Platform Consistency:** Growing a massive following is less important than maintaining a consistent, high-quality output on platforms like Substack or podcasts to build long-term relationships.

## Lessons from the Crowdsourcing Era
* **The "Crowdsourceress" Model:** Alex Daly raised over $25 million for clients (including Neil Young and Joan Didion) by leaning into early adopters and community-driven funding.
    * **Building vs. Sustaining:** Crowdfunding is excellent for building initial momentum and "belief," but brands must have a post-campaign strategy to sustain that attention.
    * **Storytelling as Capital:** Successful campaigns require the founder to be the face of the project to build human connection.
* **Venture & Funding Strategy:** Through her venture studio, **Orchard Street**, Daly advises founders to focus on building an MVP and a strong cultural infrastructure before seeking heavy outside investment.
    * **Strategic Partners:** Founders should prioritize partners who help build sustainable operations rather than just providing "white space" capital.

## The Rebirth of Long-Form and IRL Connection
* **The "Analog" Counter-Trend:** As AI drives massive efficiency and content saturation, there is a growing "doubling down" on analog experiences and long-form reading.
    * **Long-Form Content:** Despite the rise of short-form video (TikTok/Reels), audiences are carving out time for deep-dive newsletters and podcasts because they value the source.
    * **IRL (In Real Life) Strategy:** Daly recommends intimate, high-impact events over expensive marketing "stunts."
* **High-Impact Intimacy:** Spending $5,000–$10,000 on a private dinner for the right voices often yields better brand awareness and ROI than a $100,000 flash-in-the-pan activation in Times Square.

## Shaking Up Workplace Culture and AI
* **The 32-Hour Work Week:** Daly’s agency implemented a shortened work week to prioritize "happiness over revenue," proving that service-based companies can maintain client results while protecting team well-being.
* **Operational Excellence:** To manage a fully remote, 12-person team, Daly utilizes a 100-page operations manual to ensure consistency and seamless onboarding.
* **Abundance Mindset:** The agency uses biannual profit sharing and "work from anywhere" policies to retain talent and foster a culture of transparency.
* **Ethical AI Integration:**
    * **Augmentation, Not Replacement:** The agency uses AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude to handle "efficiency" tasks, freeing up humans for strategy and creativity.
    * **Strict Guardrails:** AI is never used for final drafts; it serves only as a starting point or a tool to overcome creative blocks.

> "If I have to do a lot of convincing of like your audience might not be the New York Times, it might be this Substack, this very niche community, and if they're like okay let's let's try that out, that's where we can have some fun." — Alex Daly

> "AI is making everything efficient, efficient, efficient... but on the flip side, I think that there's this like doubling down on analog and IRL... people are really craving the long form." — Alex Daly

> "I think that people don't really trust like this super polished corporate messaging. They really trust honest founders that put themselves out there. And that's what you fall in love with." — Alex Daly

**TL;DR**
India has successfully transitioned from a nation of aspirations to one of decisive execution, leveraging massive digital public infrastructure, strategic trade alliances, and aggressive policy reforms to position itself as a central pillar of the new global economic order.

## Geopolitical Strategy and Global Trade
* **Trade Diplomacy:** India concluded five transformative trade agreements within a single year, including partnerships with the US, EU, UK, New Zealand, and Oman.
    * The EU Free Trade agreement represents approximately 25% of global GDP.

* **Economic Sovereignty:** The "Atmanirbhar" (self-reliance) initiative has evolved from a local policy into a critical strategy to counter the "weaponization" of global supply chains and technology.
* **Global Leadership:** India is no longer a passive participant but an "active shaper" of the global order, guided by continuity, credibility, and conviction.

## Digital Infrastructure and Media Sovereignty
* **Population-Scale DPI:** India is the first major democracy to build population-scale digital public infrastructure across identity, payments, and governance.
    * **Digital Payments:** The nation processes over 100 billion digital transactions annually.
    * **UPI Dominance:** UPI now accounts for 85% of retail digital payments, a scale unmatched globally.
* **Tech and Media Independence:** There is an urgent need to build globally competitive Indian businesses in tech and media to counter foreign dominance.
    * **Ad Spend:** Foreign-owned businesses currently control over 60% of India’s overall advertising spend.
    * **Regulatory Frameworks:** India must establish regulations to ensure fair compensation for the media industry as AI and social media become primary consumption channels.
* **Frontier Technologies:** Decisive moves into "sovereign" tech via the India Semiconductor Mission, National Quantum Mission, and AI missions.

## Physical Infrastructure and Energy Transition
* **Transportation Growth:** 
    * Over 50,000 kilometers of national highways have been added in the last 10 years.
    * India’s metro network is now the third largest in the world, exceeding 1,000 kilometers.

briefings.title: UN Ambassador Mike Waltz Touts Gaza Plan, Board Of Peace At Munich Security Conference
briefings.tldr: US Ambassador Mike Waltz detailed a paradigm shift in American foreign policy characterized by aggressive UN budgetary reforms and the "Donroe Doctrine," prioritizing Western Hemisphere security and results-oriented "focused multilateralism" over traditional, symbolism-heavy diplomacy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
US Ambassador Mike Waltz detailed a paradigm shift in American foreign policy characterized by aggressive UN budgetary reforms and the "Donroe Doctrine," prioritizing Western Hemisphere security and results-oriented "focused multilateralism" over traditional, symbolism-heavy diplomacy.

## UN Reform and "Make the UN Great Again" (MUNGA)
*   **Budgetary Reductions:** Ambassador Mike Waltz announced the first-ever budget cut in UN history, emphasizing a "back to basics" approach to peacekeeping and peacemaking.
    *   **15% overall budget reduction** approved in December.
    *   **3,000 headquarters bureaucrats** and 18% of total personnel to be eliminated.
    *   **25% cut to peacekeeping** funds to ensure the organization is "fit for purpose."
*   **Fiscal Responsibility:** Waltz argued that US leadership in reform is mandatory because the US pays more in dues than 180 other countries combined, making the "status quo" unsustainable for American taxpayers.
*   **Operational Focus:** The US is pushing the UN to abandon its attempt to "be everything to every nation" and return to its core founding mandates.

## The "Donroe Doctrine" and Hemispheric Security
*   **Strategic Shift:** The US has articulated a "Trump corollary" to the Monroe Doctrine (termed the "Donroe Doctrine"), asserting explicit US leadership and power projection within the Western Hemisphere.
*   **Colombia’s Role:** Defense Minister Sanchez emphasized that the drug trade is a global economic scourge rather than just a local military issue.
    *   **Human Cost:** Over 2,000 Colombian military and police personnel were killed or injured in the last 3.5 years fighting the drug trade.
    *   **"Americas First":** President Petro adjusted the "America First" slogan to "Americas" (plural), signaling a desire for a continental partnership rather than US isolationism.
*   **Combatting Disinformation:** Both Waltz and Sanchez highlighted disinformation as a primary threat to regional security, noting it nearly derailed US-Colombia relations by misrepresenting Colombia’s efforts against drug cartels.

## The Gaza Plan and the "Board of Peace"
*   **Focused Multilateralism:** Waltz touted the creation of a "Board of Peace" to bypass the perceived stagnation of the UN Security Council regarding the conflict in Gaza.
    *   **Regional Inclusion:** The board involves Gulf Arab nations and Muslim-majority states, including Turkey, Pakistan, and Indonesia.
    *   **Troop Contributions:** Indonesia has publicly committed 8,000 troops to the peace efforts.
*   **Alternative to Hamas:** The strategy seeks a "third way" between Hamas rule and endless war, utilizing a Palestinian Technocratic Committee and a specialized funding mechanism.
*   **Diplomatic Wins:** Waltz cited the first direct flight between Azerbaijan and Armenia and new wheat shipments through the Caucasus as evidence that this focused approach is yielding results.

## Challenges to the New World Order
*   **Equality of States:** Estonian PM Kaja Kallas argued that while reform is necessary, the multilateral system must maintain the "equality of states" and ensure no nation is above the law.
    *   **The "Allies" Advantage:** Kallas noted that the primary difference between the US and other superpowers (like Russia or China) is the US's network of allies who choose to cooperate.
*   **Transition Risks:** Prince Faisal warned that the world is in a dangerous transition period between the old Eurocentric rules-based order and a new, yet-to-be-defined system.
*   **Shift from Symbolism:** There was a general consensus among the panel that the previous system was often an obstacle to addressing the actual drivers of conflict, favoring "symbolism over reality."

> "We’re going to get the UN back to fit for purpose... He [the President] will do for the UN what he’s done for NATO the last 10 years." — **Ambassador Mike Waltz**

> "America doesn’t just refer to the United States, it refers to the entire continent and together we can do more than separately." — **Minister Sanchez (quoting President Gustavo Petro)**

> "When Russia goes to war, they go alone because they don’t have allies. When America goes to war, a lot of us go with you... that is the difference between you and the other superpowers." — **PM Kaja Kallas**

> "I’m to some extent actually more optimistic than I was last year because we are actually having these conversations in a much more honest and transparent way... including among the friends in Europe who were the most ardent supporters of the old system." — **Prince Faisal**

briefings.title: US Pulls List of Tech Firms Linked to China’s Military | Bloomberg Tech 2/13/2026
